description: CPU-clock samples of the previous release graph: 30 BFS kernels after one 1,000,000-node graph construction.
harness:
# Platform boundary for the Dewy application benchmarks. The original
# harness uses compiler-specific raw syscalls; this uses the core's library.
size_argument = (values: str[], fallback: int) -> int:
    if values.len() < 2: return fallback
    text = values[1]
    value = 0
    loop byte in text:
        if byte < 48 or byte > 57: return fallback
        value = value * 10 + int(byte) - 48
        if value > 1000000000: return fallback
    value

clock = () -> int: time_ns()
mix = (hash: int, value: int) -> int: __floor_mod(hash * 31 + value, 1000000007)
analyzer:
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
import subprocess,bisect,re,json
root=Path('__dewycache__/task-tmp/graph-profile'); binary=root/'graph'
symbols=[]
for line in subprocess.check_output(['nm','-n',binary],text=True).splitlines():
    parts=line.split()
    if len(parts)==3 and parts[1].lower()=='t': symbols.append((int(parts[0],16),parts[2]))
addresses=[s[0] for s in symbols]
samples=Counter(int(line,16) for line in (root/'release.ips').read_text().splitlines())
functions=Counter()
for pc,count in samples.items():
    i=bisect.bisect_right(addresses,pc)-1
    name=f'{symbols[i][1]}@{symbols[i][0]:x}' if i>=0 else 'unknown'
    functions[name]+=count
print('Functions',len(samples),'unique PCs')
for name,count in functions.most_common(20): print(f'{count/samples.total()*100:.2f}%',name,count)
asm=subprocess.check_output(['objdump','-d','--no-show-raw-insn',binary],text=True)
(root/'release.asm').write_text(asm)
instructions=[]
for line in asm.splitlines():
    match=re.match(r'\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s*(.*)',line)
    if match: instructions.append((int(match[1],16),match[2]))
insaddr=[ins[0] for ins in instructions]
print('Hot instruction neighborhoods')
seen=set()
for pc,count in samples.most_common(15):
    i=bisect.bisect_right(insaddr,pc)-1
    if any(abs(i-j)<6 for j in seen):continue
    seen.add(i)
    print(f'PC {pc:x}: {count/samples.total()*100:.2f}%')
    for address,instruction in instructions[max(0,i-4):i+4]: print(f'{samples[address]:5} {address:x} {instruction}')
(root/'histogram.json').write_text(json.dumps({'samples':samples.total(),'functions':dict(functions.most_common()),'instruction_counts':{f'{pc:x}':count for pc,count in samples.most_common()}},indent=2)+'\n')
limits: Linux CPU-clock sampling, not cache-miss hardware counters. Interrupt PCs often follow the stalled instruction.
Sampling includes setup/cleanup; graph generation accounts for only 0.3% of samples.
Function labels are mapped by nm; no inlined source stack attribution.
The sampler buffers this bounded run and checks overflow/lost events; it is an experiment helper, not a streaming profiler.
